iterations.theme: Fran Petar Reizl: poduzetništvo, obitelj, vjera, glazba i potraga za obiteljskim korijenima

sections.subtitle: Od plastelina do obiteljske tvornice čokolade
sections.screenshot_description: Fran Petar Reizl opisuje svoje rano stvaralaštvo i put prema dizajnu
sections.content:
Novu epizodu podcasta **Redefinicija** voditelj **Kruno** otvara pozdravom „Hvaljen Isus i Marija i sveti Josip“. Gost je **Fran Petar Reizl**, kojega predstavlja kao poduzetnika, pokretača brenda **Reizl Snacks**, dizajnera, grafičara i glazbenika. Kao najvažnije uloge ističe one supruga i oca četvero djece. Gost zahvaljuje na pozivu i kaže da je počašćen što može biti dio „jedne sekvence dobrih podcasta“.

Kruno podsjeća da je Fran s poduzetništvom počeo vrlo mlad te ga moli da opiše svoje formativno razdoblje, sve do obiteljskog brenda **Vrsna čokolada**. Fran objašnjava da je oduvijek bio netko tko stvara. Otkad zna za sebe igrao se plastelinom i drugim materijalima, a ta se sklonost s vremenom pretvorila u dizajn. Najprije ga je upisao u srednjoj školi, a zatim i na studiju.

Nakon tri godine fakulteta shvatio je, kako kaže, da „nije stvoren samo za sjediti i nešto učiti“, nego da naučeno treba vraćati svijetu. U isto su vrijeme njegovi roditelji razmišljali o promjenama u maloj obiteljskoj tvrtki u **Sesvetama**. Zajedno su izradili projekt za **europske fondove** uz jasan dogovor: ako prođe, krenut će, a ako ne prođe, „nikom ništa“. Projekt je, kako Fran kaže, „hvala Bogu“ ne samo prošao, nego su bili i „jako obilato ohrabreni“. Tako je počela proizvodnja čokolade.

Vrsna čokolada i danas uspješno posluje i raste, što gostu posebno znači jer je riječ o domaćem, obiteljskom brendu. Kroz šest do sedam godina u toj tvrtki učio je o proizvodnim procesima, računovodstvu i svemu što poduzetnik mora proći. To ga je pripremilo za samostalan iskorak prije tri godine, kada je pokrenuo Reizl Snacks.
sections.subtitle_en: From plasticine to a family chocolate factory
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fran Petar Reizl describes his early creativity and path toward design
sections.content_en:
The host **Kruno** opens the new episode of the podcast **Redefinicija** with the greeting „Praised be Jesus and Mary and Saint Joseph“. The guest is **Fran Petar Reizl**, whom he introduces as an entrepreneur, founder of the brand **Reizl Snacks**, designer, graphic artist, and musician. As his most important roles, he highlights those of husband and father of four children. The guest thanks him for the invitation and says that he is honored to be able to be part of „a sequence of good podcasts“.

Kruno recalls that Fran started entrepreneurship very young and asks him to describe his formative period, all the way to the family brand **Vrsna čokolada**. Fran explains that he has always been someone who creates. For as long as he can remember, he played with plasticine and other materials, and that inclination turned into design over time. First he enrolled in it in high school, and then also in university studies.

After three years of university, he realized, as he says, that he „was not made just to sit and learn something“, but that what was learned should be returned to the world. At the same time, his parents were thinking about changes in the small family business in **Sesvete**. Together they created a project for **European funds** with a clear agreement: if it goes through, they will start, and if it does not go through, „no harm done“. The project, as Fran says, „thank God“ not only went through, but they were also „very abundantly encouraged“. That is how chocolate production began.

Vrsna čokolada still operates successfully and grows today, which means a great deal to the guest especially because it is a domestic, family brand. Through six to seven years in that company, he learned about production processes, accounting, and everything an entrepreneur must go through. That prepared him for an independent step forward three years ago, when he launched Reizl Snacks.

sections.subtitle: Reizl Snacks: zdravija alternativa i četiri strgana blendera
sections.screenshot_description: Gost opisuje razvoj voćnih pločica i testiranje smjese
sections.content:
Fran objašnjava da je Reizl Snacks nastao kao odgovor na nešto što u društvu nedostaje. I mladi i svi koji vole slatko, kaže, hrane se prilično nezdravo. Po njegovu mišljenju čips je pritom najmanji problem. Veći su problem proizvodi s mnogo **prikrivenih tvari** koje su štetne. Ideja je bila povezati se na nov način s ljudima koje poznaju i doći do što boljih sirovina i izvora.

Gost dodaje da mu je kao obiteljskom čovjeku drago što i njegova djeca vide čime se bavi, jer su mu i ona inspiracija. Reizl Snacks opisuje kao tvrtku, start-up i „obiteljski ponos“. Posao je zasad skroman i malen, ali raste, a tržište ga, kako kaže, lijepo prihvaća.

Na Krunino pitanje što brend proizvodi, Fran objašnjava da je Reizl Snacks počeo s čokoladama. Od njih su ipak brzo odustali zbog tehnoloških razloga. Čokolada se topi u transportu, a nisu htjeli da kupci dobiju proizvod kakav ne žele. Slijedila su testiranja, a gost i danas s nevjericom spominje da su „morali proći **četiri strgana blendera**“ dok nisu dobili idealnu smjesu.

Rezultat su **voćne pločice s adaptogenima**, tvarima koje prema gostovu opisu pomažu:
- u detoksikaciji tijela,
- u poboljšanju fokusa,
- u povećanju energije.

Pločice teže samo 20 i 30 grama. Fran ih ugrubo opisuje kao malu voćnu pločicu „punu hranjivih tvari“.
sections.subtitle_en: Reizl Snacks: a healthier alternative and four broken blenders
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest describes the development of fruit bars and the testing of the mixture
sections.content_en:
Fran explains that Reizl Snacks was created as a response to something that is missing in society. Both young people and everyone who loves sweets, he says, eat rather unhealthily. In his opinion, potato chips are the smallest problem here. A bigger problem is products with many **hidden substances** that are harmful. The idea was to connect in a new way with people they know and to reach the best possible raw materials and sources.

The guest adds that, as a family man, he is glad that his children also see what he does, because they too are his inspiration. He describes Reizl Snacks as a company, a start-up, and "family pride." The business is modest and small for now, but it is growing, and the market, as he says, is accepting it nicely.

To Kruno's question about what the brand produces, Fran explains that Reizl Snacks started with chocolates. However, they quickly gave up on them due to technological reasons. Chocolate melts in transport, and they did not want customers to receive a product they do not want. Testing followed, and the guest still mentions today with disbelief that they "had to go through **four broken blenders**" until they obtained the ideal mixture.

The result is **fruit bars with adaptogens**, substances that, according to the guest's description, help:
- in detoxifying the body,
- in improving focus,
- in increasing energy.

The bars weigh only 20 and 30 grams. Fran roughly describes them as a small fruit bar "full of nutrients."

sections.subtitle: Dizajn kao alat: i okus se mora dizajnirati
sections.screenshot_description: Fran objašnjava kako dizajn ulazi u sve sfere ljudskog života
sections.content:
Kruno pita kako Franova dizajnerska podloga utječe na razvoj proizvoda i odnos s kupcima. Gost dizajn opisuje kao „fascinantnu granu“ koja ulazi u sve aspekte ljudskog bitka. Cilj dizajna je stvoriti nešto lijepo i korisno. Da bi se to postiglo, potrebno je mnogo istraživanja, ulaženja u razne sfere društva i razumijevanja različitih ljudi. Svaki je kupac, naglašava, individua sa svojim dostojanstvom i potrebama, na koje proizvođač mora pokušati odgovoriti.

Za Reizl Snacks dizajn je bio ključan jer se, kako kaže, **i okus proizvoda mora dizajnirati**. Trebalo je i procijeniti hoće li proizvod izgledati lijepo ili ružno. Zdravi proizvodi i sušeno voće nisu baš lijepi, iako su vrlo hranjivi. Zato su bili potrebni kompromisi. Fran je svoje znanje iskoristio prije svega za **ambalažu**, koju opisuje kao atraktivnu, modernu i suvremenu, dok je sam proizvod „takav kakav je“.

Gost dodaje da je dizajn jedan od koraka koji su ga doveli do sadašnjeg trenutka. Počelo je kao dječja kreativnost, a postalo profesionalna grana njegova života. Ljudi često misle da se poslovni ljudi bave samo brojkama i postocima. Kao dizajner, međutim, vidi da mnogi zapravo rade na tome da stvore bolje uvjete za druge. U slučaju njegove tvrtke to znači pomoći ljudima da jedu kvalitetnije, odnosno **dizajnirati njihov životni stil i navike**. To naziva holističkim pogledom na posao.
sections.subtitle_en: Design as a tool: taste must also be designed
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fran explains how design enters all spheres of human life
sections.content_en:
Kruno asks how Fran's design background affects product development and the relationship with customers. The guest describes design as a "fascinating branch" that enters all aspects of human being. The goal of design is to create something beautiful and useful. In order to achieve this, a lot of research is needed, entering into various spheres of society and understanding different people. Every customer, he emphasizes, is an individual with their own dignity and needs, to which the producer must try to respond.

For Reizl Snacks, design was crucial because, as he says, **the taste of the product must also be designed**. It was also necessary to assess whether the product would look beautiful or ugly. Healthy products and dried fruit are not very beautiful, although they are very nutritious. Therefore, compromises were needed. Fran used his knowledge primarily for the **packaging**, which he describes as attractive, modern, and contemporary, while the product itself is "as it is".

The guest adds that design is one of the steps that brought him to the present moment. It began as childhood creativity, and became a professional branch of his life. People often think that business people only deal with numbers and percentages. As a designer, however, he sees that many actually work to create better conditions for others. In the case of his company, this means helping people eat better, that is, **designing their lifestyle and habits**. He calls this a holistic view of business.

sections.subtitle: Lovac u šumi i čuvarica četiri kuta kuće
sections.screenshot_description: Gost govori o podjeli uloga u braku i kršćanskim vrijednostima
sections.content:
Kruno postavlja pitanje kako uskladiti obiteljski i poslovni život. Fran ga naziva vrlo ozbiljnim pitanjem, koje je dvojbeno i često ostaje bez dobrog javnog odgovora. Kao vjernik vjeruje u **kršćanske vrijednosti**, za koje kaže da su ukorijenjene u prirodnom zakonu. U njegovoj obitelji vrijedi „običan bračni zakon“: muž radi, a žena je više s djecom. On je onaj koji je „na terenu, što bi rekli lovac u šumi“, a supruga brine o „četiri kuta kuće“ i djeci. Naglašava da je i sam vrlo aktivan s djecom, ali kad radi, onda radi.

Gost ne skriva da je takav raspored zahtjevan i da traži žrtvu od oboje. Muž se odriče vremena s djecom i ženom kako bi radio za dobro obitelji. Žena je pak često sama i traži načine kako ispuniti vrijeme i odgajati djecu u dobrom ozračju. Fran to opisuje kao **put posvećenja i svetosti**, koji je u mnogočemu neistražen. Ujedno ga vidi kao priliku da se u modernom dobu razviju dobri mehanizmi za svakodnevni život.

Kruno primjećuje da bi „lijevo-liberalni“ kritičari takav pogled mogli proglasiti toksičnim. Ipak, smatra da model funkcionira ako je riječ o dogovoru u obitelji. Problem nastaje kad muškarac taj dogovor krši i previše se posveti poslu. Fran se slaže i dodaje da neki muškarci rade previše jer su, kako kaže, „nezadovoljeni“ sami sa sobom. Svatko bi trebao raditi onoliko koliko je dobro za obitelj, za njega samog i za posao. Potrebna je **zlatna sredina**.
sections.subtitle_en: The hunter in the forest and the keeper of the four corners of the house
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about the division of roles in marriage and Christian values
sections.content_en:
Kruno asks the question of how to reconcile family and business life. Fran calls it a very serious question, which is controversial and often remains without a good public answer. As a believer, he believes in **Christian values**, which he says are rooted in natural law. In his family, the "ordinary marital law" applies: the husband works, and the wife is more with the children. He is the one who is "in the field, as they would say, a hunter in the forest," while the wife takes care of the "four corners of the house" and the children. He emphasizes that he himself is also very active with the children, but when he works, he works.

The guest does not hide that such an arrangement is demanding and requires sacrifice from both. The husband gives up time with the children and wife in order to work for the good of the family. The wife, on the other hand, is often alone and looks for ways to fill the time and raise the children in a good atmosphere. Fran describes this as a **path of sanctification and holiness**, which is in many ways unexplored. At the same time, he sees it as an opportunity to develop good mechanisms for everyday life in the modern age.

Kruno notes that "left-liberal" critics might declare such a view toxic. Nevertheless, he believes that the model works if it is an agreement within the family. The problem arises when a man violates that agreement and devotes himself too much to work. Fran agrees and adds that some men work too much because, as he says, they are "unsatisfied" with themselves. Everyone should work as much as is good for the family, for himself, and for work. A **golden mean** is needed.

sections.subtitle: Kraljevstvo Božje umjesto same karijere
sections.screenshot_description: Fran priča o odluci supruge da se posveti djeci
sections.content:
Fran naglašava da se u njegovoj obitelji radi o **velikom sporazumu**. Njegova je supruga profesorica kroatistike i filozofije i imala je uzlaznu karijeru. Kad je stiglo prvo dijete, „prvi mali mačić“, kako ga gost od milja naziva, sama je procijenila koja je njezina uloga. Danas, kaže, sve funkcionira „dosta lijepo“.

Kruno dodaje da su mu mnogi rekli kako u obitelji ništa neće funkcionirati dok muškarac i žena ne osvijeste svoje prave uloge, i s tim se slaže. Navodi i citat koji je čuo: muškarac nije pozvan graditi karijeru, nego **kraljevstvo Božje**. Prema njegovu mišljenju, i u tome treba svakodnevno ciljati zlatnu sredinu.

Fran tu misao razvija. Život traje 80 ili 90 godina i čovjek ga može proživjeti isključivo kroz karijeru, smatrajući je životnim smislom. Može i postaviti nebo kao cilj, a karijeru, koja je potrebna „za kruh svagdašnji“, iskoristiti tako da uz sebe „pokupi cijelu obitelj“. U tom je slučaju, zaključuje, bolje da se obitelj dobro raspodijeli.
sections.subtitle_en: The Kingdom of God instead of career alone
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fran talks about his wife's decision to dedicate herself to the children
sections.content_en:
Fran emphasizes that in his family it is a matter of a **great agreement**. His wife is a professor of Croatian studies and philosophy and had an upward career. When the first child arrived, „the first little kitten“, as the guest affectionately calls it, she herself assessed what her role was. Today, he says, everything functions „quite nicely“.

Kruno adds that many have told him that nothing in a family will work until the man and woman become aware of their true roles, and he agrees with that. He also cites a quote he heard: a man is not called to build a career, but the **Kingdom of God**. In his opinion, in this too one should aim for the golden mean every day.

Fran develops this thought. Life lasts 80 or 90 years and a person can live it exclusively through a career, considering it the meaning of life. One can also set heaven as the goal, and use the career, which is necessary „for daily bread“, in such a way as to „pick up the whole family“ along with oneself. In that case, he concludes, it is better that the family distributes tasks well.

sections.subtitle: Caru carevo, Bogu Božje: PDV kao dio računice
sections.screenshot_description: Gost iskreno govori o pogrešci pri osnivanju tvrtke i plaćanju PDV-a
sections.content:
Kruno navodi da se na **Konferencijama katoličkih muškaraca** na panelima o leadershipu i poduzetništvu redovito otvara tema poreza. Pita Frana kakav je odnos prema porezu imao kad je kretao praktički od ničega, s obzirom na visoka davanja. Zanima ga je li pomišljao da posluje mimo pravila ili je odlučio „dati Bogu Božje, caru carevo“.

Fran kaže da kod njega nije bilo velike dvojbe jer je znao da mora ići pravim putem. Priznaje i vlastitu pogrešku. Umjesto da posao pokrene kroz obrt ili neki mirniji oblik, odmah je osnovao **d.o.o. u sustavu PDV-a**, pa se prve dvije godine jedva snalazio. Ipak, nikada nije zapao u dugove ni prema državi ni prema suradnicima. PDV danas smatra jednim dijelom računice.

Gost otvoreno priznaje da je plaćanje PDV-a neugodno. U sebi se pita zašto se toliko bori za nešto, a onda četvrtinu daje „nečemu što ne vidi“, pa i stvarima s kojima se ne slaže nužno. Unatoč tome poštuje **Isusov naputak** o caru i Bogu i smatra ga posve konstruktivnim. Tko god radi procjenu projekta ili troškovnik, od kupovine do vođenja tvrtke, može u nju ugraditi „tu četvrtinu koja nije tvoja“. Poslovanje se, kaže, i dalje može dobro razvijati.

Na kraju prenosi „pošalicu“ hrvatskih povratnika iz **Amerike i Australije**: tko prođe test na hrvatskom tržištu, spreman je za bilo koje tržište. Fran to doživljava kao izazov. Ako uspije u Hrvatskoj, moći će i dalje. Kruno se slaže da je to „dobar test“.
sections.subtitle_en: To Caesar what is Caesar's, to God what is God's: VAT as part of the calculation
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks honestly about a mistake in founding the company and paying VAT
sections.content_en:
Kruno states that at the **Catholic Men's Conferences**, on panels about leadership and entrepreneurship, the topic of taxes is regularly raised. He asks Fran what his attitude towards taxes was when he started practically from nothing, considering the high duties. He is interested in whether he thought about doing business outside the rules or decided to „give to God what is God's, to Caesar what is Caesar's“.

Fran says that for him there was no great doubt because he knew he had to take the right path. He also admits his own mistake. Instead of starting the business through a craft business or some calmer form, he immediately founded a **d.o.o. in the VAT system**, so for the first two years he barely managed. Still, he never fell into debt either toward the state or toward collaborators. Today, he considers VAT to be one part of the calculation.

The guest openly admits that paying VAT is unpleasant. Within himself, he wonders why he fights so hard for something, and then gives a quarter to „something he does not see“, including things he does not necessarily agree with. Despite this, he respects **Jesus' instruction** about Caesar and God and considers it entirely constructive. Whoever makes a project estimate or bill of quantities, from purchasing to running a company, can incorporate into it „that quarter that is not yours“. Business, he says, can still develop well.

In the end, he shares a „joke“ of Croatian returnees from **America and Australia**: whoever passes the test on the Croatian market is ready for any market. Fran experiences this as a challenge. If he succeeds in Croatia, he will be able to go further. Kruno agrees that this is a „good test“.

sections.subtitle: Talenti kao Božji alat i strah od propuštene prilike
sections.screenshot_description: Fran govori o pozivu, talentima i želji da bude primjer svojoj djeci
sections.content:
Kruno pita što Frana svakog jutra pokreće da bude kreativan i odakle mu ideje za nove proizvode, s obzirom na veliku konkurenciju i brojne „omče“ i „utege“ u poduzetništvu. Fran kaže da je pitanje jednostavno, ali odgovor složen. Pokreće ga kombinacija **poziva koji mu je Bog dao** i talenata koje je dobio. Dugo mu je trebalo da shvati kako ono što je smatrao maštom i fantazijom zapravo jest njegov alat, koji mora koristiti.

Važan je i obiteljski motiv. U braku je šest, gotovo sedam godina i ima četvero djece. Svakodnevno ga potiče misao da će jednog dana biti stariji i gledati ih. Kao otac želi da u njemu vide primjer nekoga „tko nije savršen, ali tko se trudio svaki dan“.

Otkrivajući ljepotu **Božjeg stvaralaštva** u svom životu, u tuđim životima i u svijetu, Fran vidi koliko svatko ima toga dati. Priznaje da se čak boji kako bi bio velik propust kad ne bi reagirao na vrijeme i pustio da ideja „samo tako odleprša“. Poziva se na **Isusovu prispodobu o talentima**. Prva dvojica sluga imala su u sebi „mot“, kako bi rekli na jugu, i krenula raditi. Treći se bojao i propustio priliku pred nosom. To mu je pokretač, ali i način da Bogu zahvali za ono što ima.

Gost dodaje da mnogi poduzetnici vjernici koje poznaje svako jutro razmatraju i mole te se trude živjeti sakramentalno. Ljudi izvana često misle da im se „posrećilo“. Iza uspjeha je, međutim, mnogo plakanja, briga, raspisivanja ideja, dvojbi i **neisplaćenih kredita**, jer žele napraviti nešto bolje od postojećeg stanja. „Dugi odgovor na kratko pitanje“, zaključuje Fran.
sections.subtitle_en: Talents as God's Tool and the Fear of a Missed Opportunity
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fran speaks about calling, talents, and the desire to be an example to his children
sections.content_en:
Kruno asks what drives Fran every morning to be creative and where his ideas for new products come from, given the great competition and numerous “nooses” and “weights” in entrepreneurship. Fran says that the question is simple, but the answer is complex. He is driven by a combination of the **calling God gave him** and the talents he received. It took him a long time to realize that what he considered imagination and fantasy is actually his tool, which he must use.

The family motive is also important. He has been married for six, almost seven years and has four children. Every day he is motivated by the thought that one day he will be older and look at them. As a father, he wants them to see in him an example of someone “who is not perfect, but who tried hard every day”.

Discovering the beauty of **God's creativity** in his own life, in other people's lives, and in the world, Fran sees how much everyone has to give. He admits that he is even afraid that it would be a great failure if he did not react in time and let an idea “just flutter away like that”. He refers to **Jesus' parable of the talents**. The first two servants had the “drive” in them, as they would say in the south, and set to work. The third was afraid and missed the opportunity right before his eyes. That is a driver for him, but also a way to thank God for what he has.

The guest adds that many believer entrepreneurs whom he knows meditate and pray every morning and strive to live sacramentally. People from the outside often think that they “got lucky”. Behind success, however, is a lot of crying, worries, writing out ideas, doubts, and **unpaid loans**, because they want to make something better than the existing state. “A long answer to a short question,” Fran concludes.

sections.subtitle: Lekcija od tri kćeri: djeca uče ljubav gledajući roditelje
sections.screenshot_description: Gost citira Chestertona o braku kao borbi
sections.content:
Kruno podsjeća da je Franu nedavno stigao četvrti dijete, sin, „napokon, nakon tri djevojčice“. Pita ga koju je najvažniju lekciju naučio u godinama očinstva.

Fran odgovara da je naučio kako će djeca, ako će ljubav od ikoga dobiti, dobiti je od mame i tate. Što je ljubav naučit će također gledajući roditelje i njihov međusobni odnos. Nije tajna, kaže, da je brak „jedno veliko bojno polje“. Citira **Chestertona**, koji je rekao da nitko ne bi trebao ustuknuti pred izazovom braka jer je to doista „borba do smrti“. Fran dodaje: „I doista je.“

Kao najveću lekciju ističe to da djeci mora biti **autentičan i s njima u istini**. Ne očekuje da mu to uzvrate, nego se nada da će to jednog dana moći učiniti na svoj način, za svoje dobro.
sections.subtitle_en: A lesson from three daughters: children learn love watching parents
sections.screenshot_description_en: Guest cites Chesterton on marriage as a battle
sections.content_en:
Kruno recalls that Fran recently had a fourth child arrive, a son, “finally, after three girls”. He asks him what the most important lesson he learned in his years of fatherhood is.

Fran replies that he learned that children, if they will receive love from anyone, will receive it from mom and dad. What love is they will also learn watching their parents and their mutual relationship. It is no secret, he says, that marriage is “one big battlefield”. He cites **Chesterton**, who said that no one should shrink before the challenge of marriage because it is truly a “fight to the death”. Fran adds: “And it truly is.”

As the greatest lesson he highlights that for the children he must be **authentic and with them in truth**. He does not expect them to return that to him, but hopes that one day they will be able to do so in their own way, for their own good.

sections.subtitle: Muževnost kao časno držanje i mudrost znati kada krenuti
sections.screenshot_description: Fran definira muževnost u poslovnom svijetu
sections.content:
Kruno primjećuje da je poslovni svijet uglavnom obojan na muški način. Pita Frana što za njega znači biti muževan u poduzetništvu i leadershipu. Gost kaže da se danas na taj pojam gleda čudno, kao na „čudnovatog kljunaša“ ili „jednoroga, neko mitsko biće“. Mnogi muškarci koje susreće povukli su se u svoju sigurnu zonu. Fali im „kičme“, kako se kaže u narodu, i hrabrosti da stanu iza svojeg „da“ i svojeg „ne“.

Fran kaže da pažljivo bira društvo u poslovnom svijetu. Prema iskustvu s ljudima s kojima se druži, muževnost opisuje kao **časno držanje radi dobra drugih** i bratski stav. Podsjeća da je poduzetništvo često razmjena dobara i da svatko nešto treba. Primjer uzima iz vlastitog posla. Kad traži voće za svoj proizvod, onaj od koga ga traži mora od njega dobiti poštovanje. Uz plaćanje, to znači i ljudsku stranu, primjerice lijepu riječ.

Muževnost vidi i kao nešto što nije podložno političkim pitanjima ni vrijednostima koje „dolaze pa prolaze“. Biti muževan znači biti **čvrsto ukopan u tlu**. Kad bi svi htjeli krenuti, muškarac zna da nije vrijeme. Kad svi stoje, zna krenuti. Zato je **mudrost** po njegovu mišljenju velika sastavnica muževnosti.

U osobnoj noti gost se sjeća predaka o kojima je slušao priče i načina na koji su reagirali u izazovnim situacijama. Spominje i starozavjetne svece i velikane vjere koji su pokazali što znači biti muževan. Upravo to želi prenijeti u svoju poslovnu karijeru.
sections.subtitle_en: Masculinity as Honorable Bearing and the Wisdom to Know When to Move
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fran defines masculinity in the business world
sections.content_en:
Kruno notes that the business world is largely colored in a masculine way. He asks Fran what being masculine in entrepreneurship and leadership means to him. The guest says that today that term is viewed strangely, like a "platypus" or "a unicorn, some mythical creature." Many men he meets have retreated into their comfort zone. They lack "backbone," as the saying goes among the people, and the courage to stand behind their "yes" and their "no."

Fran says he carefully chooses his company in the business world. According to his experience with the people he associates with, he describes masculinity as **honorable bearing for the good of others** and a brotherly attitude. He recalls that entrepreneurship is often an exchange of goods and that everyone needs something. He takes an example from his own business. When he is looking for fruit for his product, the person he is asking it from must receive respect from him. Alongside payment, that also means the human side, for example, a kind word.

He also sees masculinity as something that is not subject to political questions or values that "come and go." Being masculine means being **firmly dug into the ground**. When everyone would want to move, a man knows that it is not the time. When everyone stands still, he knows to move. That is why **wisdom**, in his opinion, is a major component of masculinity.

On a personal note, the guest remembers his ancestors about whom he heard stories and the way they reacted in challenging situations. He also mentions Old Testament saints and giants of faith who showed what it means to be masculine. It is precisely this that he wants to carry over into his business career.

sections.subtitle: Nedostaje kultura poticanja: „Bravo, brate, kreni!“
sections.screenshot_description: Gost prenosi razgovor s hrvatskim povratnikom koji je radio u Boeingu
sections.content:
Kruno pita s kojim se izazovima danas najviše susreću mladi poduzetnici u Hrvatskoj. Fran prepričava razgovor koji je istog dana imao s Hrvatom povratnikom iz **New Yorka**, koji je radio u **Boeingu**. Sugovornik mu je rekao da su Hrvati koji su otišli u inozemstvo i željeli uspjeti uglavnom natprosječno uspješni jer u sebi imaju borbenost i stav. Oni koji su ostali u Hrvatskoj, smatra gost, često zaborave da se i ovdje moraju boriti i da imaju razloga za samopouzdanje i razvijanje sposobnosti.

Kao objektivne teškoće navodi visok **PDV** i nedostatak poticaja. Financijski poticaji, uključujući one **Europske unije**, postoje. Ono što nedostaje jest poticaj na ljudskoj razini, da netko kaže: „Bravo, brate, kreni, stisni zube, izdrži dvije godine i vidjet ćeš gdje ćeš biti.“ Fali **kultura poticanja**, u kojoj bi otac rekao sinu da krene smjerom koji je zacrtao jer je možda bolji od njegova. Umjesto toga, kaže Fran, često se „povlači za rukav“ uz upozorenja da će se zadužiti i upropastiti sebe i obitelj.

Ipak, vjeruje da ova generacija ima priliku to promijeniti. Velika joj je prednost mnoštvo dobrog i besplatnog sadržaja sa Zapada, osobito o ekonomiji i poduzetništvu, u kojem uspješni ljudi objašnjavaju svoje puteve. Ti su putevi, kaže, „de facto svima isti“: svi krenu od ničega, a ključna je borba. „Tko dulje bude trajao, taj će više toga i postići.“ Hrvatskoj po njegovu mišljenju nedostaje **dugoročni fokus**. Nešto se možda neće riješiti za godinu-dvije, nego za pet, ali nakon pet godina čovjek je već napravio natprosječno mnogo.
sections.subtitle_en: A culture of encouragement is missing: „Bravo, brother, go for it!“
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest recounts a conversation with a Croatian returnee who worked at Boeing
sections.content_en:
Kruno asks what challenges young entrepreneurs in Croatia face the most today. Fran recounts a conversation he had that same day with a Croatian returnee from **New York**, who worked at **Boeing**. His interlocutor told him that Croats who went abroad and wanted to succeed are mostly above-average successful because they have fighting spirit and attitude within them. Those who stayed in Croatia, the guest believes, often forget that they must fight here as well and that they have reasons for self-confidence and developing their abilities.

As objective difficulties, he cites high **VAT** and a lack of encouragement. Financial incentives, including those of the **European Union**, do exist. What is missing is encouragement on a human level, for someone to say: „Bravo, brother, go for it, grit your teeth, hold on for two years and you will see where you will be.“ A **culture of encouragement** is missing, in which a father would tell his son to head in the direction he charted because it might be better than his own. Instead, Fran says, one is often „pulled by the sleeve“ with warnings that they will go into debt and ruin themselves and their family.

Still, he believes that this generation has an opportunity to change that. Its great advantage is a multitude of good and free content from the West, especially about economics and entrepreneurship, in which successful people explain their paths. Those paths, he says, are „de facto the same for everyone“: everyone starts from nothing, and the key is the struggle. „Whoever lasts longer will also achieve more.“ In his opinion, Croatia lacks a **long-term focus**. Something might not be resolved in a year or two, but in five, but after five years a person has already accomplished an above-average amount.

sections.subtitle: Zavist, „naysayeri“ i Hrvatska koja bi mogla biti Švicarska
sections.screenshot_description: Fran govori o manjku liderstva i nadi u procvat hrvatskog poduzetništva
sections.content:
Kruno nadovezuje da su oko onoga tko kreće u nešto novo obično „naysayeri“, ljudi koji govore: „Nemoj nikako, izgubit ćeš glavu.“ Kao još jednu kočnicu hrvatskog poduzetništva vidi negativnost, a možda i **zavist**. Ako netko krene, drugi će vidjeti da je moguće, pa će i sami morati krenuti. Smatra da previše i previše negativno razmišljamo. S našim talentima i potrebama društva, zaključuje, možemo uspješno odgovoriti na izazove samo ako se malo odvažimo.

Fran se slaže i ponavlja ono što je, kako kaže, govorio i drugdje: Hrvatska je sredina koja bi vrlo lako mogla postati **Švicarska** kad bi to htjela i kad bi imala odgovarajuće liderstvo. Hrvatsko je liderstvo po njegovu sudu generalno loše jer nedostaje ljudi sa stavom, koji se neće podlagati drugima i koji će preuzeti rizike. To je jedan od razloga zašto nije onoliko lako koliko bi moglo biti.

Potvrđuje da su sumnja, nepoticanje i ljubomora definitivno prisutni. Razgovarajući sa starijim, srednjim i mlađim generacijama, kao i s najmlađima koji tek kreću, ipak vidi da stvari idu u dobrom smjeru. Nada se da će se to iskristalizirati i da će Hrvatska doživjeti **procvat**. Kruno se tome iskreno pridružuje.
sections.subtitle_en: Envy, "Naysayers", and a Croatia That Could Be Switzerland
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fran speaks about the lack of leadership and the hope for the flourishing of Croatian entrepreneurship
sections.content_en:
Kruno adds that around someone starting something new there are usually "naysayers", people who say: "Don't do it at all, you'll lose your head." As another brake on Croatian entrepreneurship, he sees negativity, and perhaps **envy**. If someone starts, others will see that it is possible, so they will have to start themselves too. He believes that we think too much and too negatively. With our talents and the needs of society, he concludes, we can successfully respond to challenges only if we dare a little.

Fran agrees and repeats what he, as he says, has said elsewhere too: Croatia is an environment that could very easily become **Switzerland** if it wanted to and if it had adequate leadership. Croatian leadership, in his judgment, is generally poor because there is a lack of people with conviction, who will not subordinate themselves to others and who will take risks. That is one of the reasons why it is not as easy as it could be.

He confirms that doubt, lack of encouragement, and jealousy are definitely present. Talking with older, middle, and younger generations, as well as with the youngest who are just starting out, he nevertheless sees that things are moving in a good direction. He hopes that this will crystallize and that Croatia will experience a **flourishing**. Kruno sincerely joins in this.

sections.subtitle: Jedna navika, dvije „navikice“: razgovor, rano ustajanje i tišina
sections.screenshot_description: Gost preporučuje razgovor s ljudima od povjerenja i jutarnju tišinu
sections.content:
Na pitanje koju bi naviku preporučio onima koji kreću u poduzetništvo, Fran kaže da je to jedna navika koja povlači još barem dvije „podnaviknice“. Osnovna je navika **puno razgovarati s ljudima u koje imaš pouzdanja**, s onima koji su te dosad poticali i donosili ti vrijednost. S njima treba razglabati ideje kako bi dali dodatni input. Mnogo komunikacije o jednoj temi, objašnjava, otvara mnoga vrata da se plan ostvari u stvarnosti. „Što više vrtimo, to se više šansa povećava.“

To podrazumijeva i određeni životni tempo:
- **ranije ustajanje**,
- **razmišljanje u tišini** prije početka posla,
- raspisivanje misli i njihovo iznošenje pred nekoga od povjerenja.

U tišini i samoći, kaže gost, čovjek puno bolje čuje sam sebe. Najprije treba osvijestiti koje su to misli i zašto se javljaju, zapisati ih, a zatim „staviti na stol“ pred nekoga i prokomentirati. Iako priznaje da je malo zakomplicirao, sažima: teme treba prodiskutirati s onima kojima vjerujemo, jer se tako povećava šansa za uspjeh.

Kruno dodaje da se treba okružiti pametnijima i iskusnijima od sebe. Ljudi se često okružuju onima koji ništa ne znaju o njihovu poslu i koji im „tu i tamo zaplješću“. Zapravo su potrebni **mentori**, od kojih se može učiti. Fran se slaže: „Točno to.“
sections.subtitle_en: One habit, two "little habits": conversation, getting up early, and silence
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest recommends conversation with trusted people and morning silence
sections.content_en:
To the question of which habit he would recommend to those embarking on entrepreneurship, Fran says that it is one habit that entails at least two "sub-habits". The basic habit is **to talk a lot with people you trust**, with those who have encouraged you so far and brought you value. One should discuss ideas with them so they can provide additional input. A lot of communication about one topic, he explains, opens many doors for the plan to be realized in reality. "The more we turn it over, the more the chance increases."

This also implies a certain rhythm of life:
- **getting up earlier**,
- **thinking in silence** before the start of work,
- writing out thoughts and presenting them before someone trusted.

In silence and solitude, says the guest, a person hears himself much better. First, one needs to become aware of what those thoughts are and why they arise, write them down, and then "put them on the table" before someone and comment on them. Although he admits he made it a bit complicated, he summarizes: topics should be discussed with those we trust, because that increases the chance of success.

Kruno adds that one should surround oneself with those smarter and more experienced than oneself. People often surround themselves with those who know nothing about their work and who "applaud them here and there". What is actually needed are **mentors**, from whom one can learn. Fran agrees: "Exactly that."

sections.subtitle: San iz srednje škole: kršćanski alternativni rock-pop bend
sections.screenshot_description: Fran priča o počecima benda i pomoći don Damira Stojića
sections.content:
Kruno zatim prelazi na još jedan Franov talent, glazbu, i pita kako je nastao bend, što su postigli i kakvi su planovi. Fran kaže da je bend bio njegova srednjoškolska ljubav i „san snova“. Bio je i ostao veliki obožavatelj benda **U2**, koji mu je uvijek bio inspirativan. S vremenom su mu se, kaže, malo udaljili „zbog vrijednosti koje zastupaju“, ali je stara inačica benda bila dobra. Kruno dobacuje: „Dok je trajalo.“

Sve je krenulo iz kreativne podloge. Osjetio je da, kad sjedne za stol s papirom, može napisati rime. Tek je kasnije shvatio koliko se dubokih stvari može staviti u nekoliko rečenica pjesme. Mudrost je, kaže, u tome da se vrijednosti i poruke sažmu u što manje teksta, a vjeruje da je i psalmist imao s tim muke. Fran je završio osnovnu glazbenu školu za klavir, dok je gitaru svladao kao samouk. Uslijedili su prijatelji i zajedničko sviranje pred drugim prijateljima.

Veliki odskok dogodio se prije petnaestak godina, dok je bio u srednjoj školi. Zasluge pripisuje zagrebačkim **salezijancima**, konkretno **don Damiru Stojiću**. On je čuo njihove pjesme, usmjerio ih u studio i potaknuo da traže donacije. Tako su nastale prve pjesme, koje već petnaest godina stoje na **YouTubeu**.

Ideja je bila stvoriti **alternativni rock-pop kršćanski katolički bend**. Projekt je, međutim, financijski zahtjevan i teško ga je pokrenuti, a kamoli održavati dugoročno. Zato Fran objavljuje stvari povremeno, kad su okolnosti povoljne. Cilj je **album od 12 pjesama**, za koji je sav sadržaj gotov, ali se čeka pravi trenutak. Stigla je beba, posao se razvio, pa je hobi morao privremeno ostaviti po strani. Ipak vjeruje da će album biti vrijedan kad izađe.
sections.subtitle_en: High school dream: Christian alternative rock-pop band
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fran talks about the band's beginnings and the help of don Damir Stojić
sections.content_en:
Kruno then moves on to another of Fran's talents, music, and asks how the band was formed, what they achieved, and what the plans are. Fran says that the band was his high school love and a "dream of dreams." He was and remained a big fan of the band **U2**, which was always inspiring to him. Over time, he says, they grew a bit distant to him "due to the values they represent," but the old version of the band was good. Kruno quips: "While it lasted."

Everything started from a creative foundation. He felt that when he sits at a table with paper, he can write rhymes. Only later did he realize how many deep things can be put into a few sentences of a song. Wisdom lies, he says, in summarizing values and messages into as little text as possible, and he believes that the psalmist also struggled with that. Fran finished elementary music school for piano, while he mastered the guitar as self-taught. Friends followed, and playing together in front of other friends.

The big leap happened about fifteen years ago, while he was in high school. He attributes the credit to the Zagreb **Salesians**, specifically **don Damir Stojić**. He heard their songs, directed them to a studio, and encouraged them to seek donations. That is how the first songs were created, which have been on **YouTube** for fifteen years.

The idea was to create an **alternative rock-pop Christian Catholic band**. The project is, however, financially demanding and difficult to launch, let alone maintain long-term. That is why Fran publishes things occasionally, when circumstances are favorable. The goal is a **12-song album**, for which all the content is finished, but waiting for the right moment. A baby arrived, work developed, so the hobby had to be temporarily set aside. Still, he believes that the album will be worthwhile when it comes out.

sections.subtitle: „Stvori me“: pjesma o čovjeku kojega Bog stvara iz pepela
sections.screenshot_description: Gost objašnjava poruku svoje najdraže pjesme
sections.content:
Kruno ističe da bi bila šteta ne okruniti sve to „pozitivnim, lijepim, solidnim albumom“ i pita koja je Franu najdraža pjesma. Gost odgovara da je to **„Stvori me“**, koja je bend i „pogurala naprijed među ljude“. Refren ukratko glasi „Stvori me iz pepela“.

Fran objašnjava poruku. Stvarnost je surova i čovjek se često osjeća nebitnim, kao da ga nitko ne doživljava. Proživljava niz neugodnih iskustava s ljudima oko sebe i s društvom, a izvana stiže previše loših informacija, pa se čini da ga svatko želi poniziti. Na kraju se čovjek treba oporaviti i vratiti onome izvornom iz **Knjige Postanka**, gdje Bog stvara čovjeka iz pepela.

Pjesmu je napisao s otprilike 18 godina. Kad ju je nedavno ponovno poslušao, učinila mu se toliko dobrom kao da je nije on napisao. „Čija je to pjesma?“, šali se Kruno, a Fran iskustvo opisuje kao nadrealno, kao čudan déjà vu. Priznaje da mu to nije jedina najdraža pjesma. Još nekoliko pjesama koje tek trebaju izaći bit će mu, kako kaže, „the ones“. Kruno odgovara da jedva čeka, on i supruga, a vjeruje i velika zajednica obožavatelja.
sections.subtitle_en: "Create Me": a song about a man whom God creates from ashes
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains the message of his favorite song
sections.content_en:
Kruno points out that it would be a pity not to crown all that with a "positive, beautiful, solid album" and asks what Fran's favorite song is. The guest replies that it is **"Create Me"**, which also "pushed the band forward among people". The chorus briefly goes "Create me from ashes".

Fran explains the message. Reality is harsh and man often feels insignificant, as if no one pays attention to him. He goes through a series of unpleasant experiences with the people around him and with society, and too much bad information comes from the outside, so it seems that everyone wants to humiliate him. In the end, man needs to recover and return to that original thing from the **Book of Genesis**, where God creates man from ashes.

He wrote the song at about 18 years old. When he listened to it again recently, it seemed so good to him as if he had not written it himself. "Whose song is that?", Kruno jokes, and Fran describes the experience as surreal, like a strange déjà vu. He admits that it is not his only favorite song. A few more songs that are yet to come out will be, as he says, "the ones" for him. Kruno replies that he can hardly wait, he and his wife, and he believes a large community of fans as well.

sections.subtitle: S djetetom u naručju na groblju: kako je počela potraga za korijenima
sections.screenshot_description: Fran opisuje trenutak na groblju koji ga je potaknuo na istraživanje porijekla
sections.content:
Kruno spominje Franov velik interes za povijest i njegovo izlaganje na **četvrtoj Konferenciji katoličkih muškaraca u Lovranu**, naslovljeno **„Korijenje prošlosti za plodove budućnosti“**. Ondje je gost predstavio svoju obiteljsku priču. Kruno ga moli da ispriča kako je taj interes počeo i što je otkrio.

Fran kaže da svi odnekud potječemo. Kad čovjek dobije djecu, shvati da će i ona jednog dana dobiti svoju i da tako ide u nedogled, ali i unatrag. Povijest najčešće gledamo kroz političke okolnosti, previranja, ratove i nepravde. Takva povijest zna biti „bez nade“, „šturа i suhoparna“.

Prekretnica je došla nakon rođenja i krštenja jednog od njegove djece. Za **Sve svete** otišao je s djetetom u naručju na groblje i shvatio da dolazi k nekome koga nikad nije upoznao, a tko je „njegov“. Tada je osjetio da mora shvatiti kako su došli do mjesta na kojem jesu. Prezime zvuči germanski i obitelj često zadirkuju da su Nijemci. Zapravo su, otkrit će, podrijetlom **Česi od prije osam generacija**. „Hrvati smo, ali smo davno, davno bili Česi“, pojašnjava.

U mirnijem razdoblju nakon **zagrebačkog potresa** i za vrijeme **korone** javio se ljudima za koje je znao da mu mogu pomoći. Ključan je bio **profesor Vjenceslav Herout**, koji je njegovu ocu predavao u školi još sedamdesetih. On ga je uveo u priču i pokazao mu cijeli svoj opus o tome odakle su ti preci došli, tko su bili i zašto su došli.
sections.subtitle_en: With a child in his arms at the cemetery: how the search for roots began
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fran describes the moment at the cemetery that prompted him to research his origin
sections.content_en:
Kruno mentions Fran's great interest in history and his presentation at the **fourth Conference of Catholic Men in Lovran**, titled **"Roots of the Past for the Fruits of the Future"**. There, the guest presented his family story. Kruno asks him to recount how that interest began and what he discovered.

Fran says that we all come from somewhere. When a person has children, he realizes that they will also one day have their own, and that it goes on endlessly like that, but also backward. We most often view history through political circumstances, turmoil, wars, and injustices. Such history can be "without hope", "scant and dry".

The turning point came after the birth and baptism of one of his children. For **All Saints**, he went with the child in his arms to the cemetery and realized that he was coming to someone he had never met, but who is "his". Then he felt that he had to understand how they arrived at the place where they are. The surname sounds Germanic and the family is often teased about being Germans. In fact, he would discover, they are by origin **Czechs from eight generations ago**. "We are Croats, but long, long ago we were Czechs", he explains.

In the calmer period after the **Zagreb earthquake** and during **corona**, he reached out to people who he knew could help him. Key was **Professor Vjenceslav Herout**, who taught his father in school back in the seventies. He introduced him to the story and showed him his entire opus about where those ancestors came from, who they were, and why they came.
entities_en: Roots of the Past for the Fruits of the Future

sections.subtitle: Graničari, pješaci i obiteljska kronika koja pamti i bake
sections.screenshot_description: Gost objašnjava značenje prezimena i češke pretke graničare
sections.content:
Istraživanje je pokazalo da su Franovi preci bili **graničari** u vrijeme borbi s Turcima. Kad je Slavonija postupno oslobođena, pozivani su ljudi koji će ondje stražariti. Došlo je oko **petsto Čeha**, cijelo selo, a kao protuvrijednost za čuvanje granice dobili su zemlju. Upoznajući sve više stručnjaka, Fran je istraživanje doveo do **kasnog srednjeg vijeka**, „od djeda do djeda“.

Otkrio je i značenje prezimena, koje nema uporište u hrvatskom, nego u njemačkom jeziku, a značilo je **„pješak, vojnik“**. Ta mu je simbolika draga iz tri razloga. Takav je izvor prezimena, preci su bili graničari, a danas se i sam osjeća kao da brani dostojanstvo svoje obitelji i domovine u kojoj i za koju živi. Zato smatra da bi svatko trebao otkriti svoje korijene. Upozorava ipak da to traži „užasno puno vremena“ i da nije preporučljivo mladima. On je, kaže, imao taj luksuz.

Plod istraživanja bit će **interna obiteljska knjiga**, opsežna kronika koja neće biti javna, a pojasnit će odakle je obitelj potekla. Posebnost je u tome što nije istraživao samo očevu lozu. Popisao je **sve žene**, i s majčine i sa svoje strane, jer je htio znati koje su bake postojale prije njega. Sada ima kćeri i želi i njima to ispričati.

Veliku inspiraciju bila mu je **pokojna prabaka**. Pričala mu je o svojim bakama rođenima 1840-ih, kojih se sjećala. Franu je nevjerojatno da mu netko tko je živio u njegovo vrijeme može pričati o ljudima od prije 170 godina, iz **doba Jelačića**, kao da je bilo jučer. To vidi kao crtu koja spaja nebo i zemlju.
sections.subtitle_en: Frontiersmen, infantrymen, and a family chronicle that remembers grandmothers too
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains the meaning of the surname and Czech frontiersmen ancestors
sections.content_en:
Research showed that Fran's ancestors were **frontiersmen** during the time of fighting with the Turks. When Slavonija was gradually liberated, people were invited to stand guard there. About **five hundred Czechs** arrived, an entire village, and in exchange for guarding the border, they received land. Meeting more and more experts, Fran took the research back to the **late Middle Ages**, „from grandfather to grandfather”.

He also discovered the meaning of the surname, which has no basis in the Croatian, but in the German language, and meant **„infantryman, soldier”**. That symbolism is dear to him for three reasons. Such is the origin of the surname, the ancestors were frontiersmen, and today he himself feels as if he is defending the dignity of his family and homeland in which and for which he lives. That is why he considers that everyone should discover their roots. He warns, however, that this takes „a terrible amount of time” and is not recommended for young people. He had, he says, that luxury.

The fruit of the research will be an **internal family book**, an extensive chronicle that will not be public, and it will explain where the family originated from. The special feature is that he did not investigate only the paternal lineage. He recorded **all the women**, both on his mother's side and on his own side, because he wanted to know which grandmothers existed before him. Now he has daughters and wants to tell this to them as well.

A great inspiration to him was his **late great-grandmother**. She told him about her grandmothers born in the 1840s, whom she remembered. To Fran it is incredible that someone who lived in his time can tell him about people from 170 years ago, from the **era of Jelačić**, as if it were yesterday. He sees this as a line that connects heaven and earth.

sections.subtitle: Demokracija živih i mrtvih: svi smo braća i sestre
sections.screenshot_description: Fran govori o Bogu Ocu kao izvoru i povezanosti svih Hrvata
sections.content:
Fran se ponovno poziva na **Chestertona**, koji je rekao da živimo u „demokraciji neba i zemlje, odnosno živih i mrtvih“. Treba osvijestiti da Crkvu čine i oni koji su ovdje i oni koji su na nebu, „daj Bože da i mi jednog dana“. Smatra to nužnim dijelom razumijevanja vlastitog identiteta za svakoga tko može ići tim putem.

Najveće otkriće cijelog istraživanja, kaže gost, bilo je da je izvor svih tih ljudi zapravo **Bog Otac** i da smo ukorijenjeni u njemu. To znači da smo **svi braća i sestre**. Kad to shvati, čovjeku se automatski mijenja pristup drugima jer zna da je svakome „nešto u nekom tamo koljenu“.

Za Hrvate to posebno vrijedi. Po Franovu mišljenju svi smo rođaci „u petnaestom, šesnaestom koljenu“ jer smo premalen narod da bismo bili nepovezani. Navodi primjere:
- Slavonija je puna Hercegovaca,
- Lika je puna Bosanaca,
- Dubrovnik je pun ljudi iz srednje Bosne.

Svi smo, zaključuje, „drevno izmiješan narod“, i to je dobro jer zbog toga možemo biti bolji i bliži. Kruno dodaje: „Svi smo braća i sestre u Kristu.“ Fran potvrđuje: „U Kristu, na kraju krajeva.“
sections.subtitle_en: Democracy of the living and the dead: we are all brothers and sisters
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fran speaks about God the Father as the source and connection of all Croats
sections.content_en:
Fran again refers to **Chesterton**, who said that we live in a "democracy of heaven and earth, that is, of the living and the dead." One needs to become aware that the Church is made up of both those who are here and those who are in heaven, "God grant that we may be one day too." He considers this a necessary part of understanding one's own identity for anyone who can take that path.

The greatest discovery of the entire research, says the guest, was that the source of all these people is actually **God the Father** and that we are rooted in him. This means that we are **all brothers and sisters**. When one realizes this, a person's approach to others automatically changes because one knows that they are "something to everyone in some generation or other."

For Croats, this is especially true. In Fran's opinion, we are all relatives "in the fifteenth, sixteenth generation" because we are too small a nation to be unconnected. He gives examples:
- Slavonija is full of Herzegovinians,
- Lika is full of Bosnians,
- Dubrovnik is full of people from central Bosnia.

We are all, he concludes, an "anciently mixed nation," and that is good because of that we can be better and closer. Kruno adds: "We are all brothers and sisters in Christ." Fran confirms: "In Christ, after all."

sections.subtitle: 1360 prezimena koja su prošla ispod radara
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj Kruno govori o svojoj knjizi o prezimenima i slabom interesu javnosti
sections.content:
Kruno otkriva da ga je razočaralo što mnoge ljude ta tema ne zanima. Deset godina radio je na doktoratu koji se, između ostalog, bavi imenima i prezimenima njegova kraja, **Poklončićkog prigorja**. Iz rada je nastala i knjiga **„Prezimena Poklončićkog prigorja“**. Mislio je da će je ljudi „razgrabiti“. Nije računao na zaradu, nego na interes. Knjiga je ipak „prošla ispod radara“: tek tu i tamo netko pita za nju ili pogleda svoje prezime.

U knjizi je obradio **1360 prezimena**, s prvom pojavom, grafijom, značenjem, etimologijom i motivacijom. Prezimena su, kaže, toliko zanimljiva i toliko toga govore, a mnoge „nije briga“. Kruno smatra da čovjek mora znati odakle je došao jer to na neki način pokazuje i kamo ide. Podrijetlo ne zacrtava put, ali je velik poticaj. Ipak, Franova i druge slične priče ohrabruju ga da nije pisao samo za sebe.

Fran upozorava na fenomen u **Americi**, gdje raste cijeli val istraživača **genealogije**. Ondje su svi odnekud došli, a mnogi ne znaju odakle. Vjeruje da će se to postupno dogoditi i u Hrvatskoj jer svi mislimo da smo „samo“ ono što jesmo. On je mislio da su mu svi preci Slavonci, a ispostavilo se da su Česi. „Svi smo odnekuda.“

Iz istraživanja je izvukao i veliku lekciju. Treba se ponositi podrijetlom, ali **ne površno**. Svaki rod nosi svoj teret, pa i „grijehe starine“. S druge strane, ne treba ni živjeti pod tim bremenom jer na davna vremena više ne možemo utjecati. Ono što možemo jest zahvaliti Bogu za svakoga tko je postojao i dopustio da se rodi sljedeći, sve do nas. Da samo jedna osoba nije bila u tom lancu, „nas vjerojatno ne bi bilo“. To je, kaže gost, čudo, i upravo zato vrijedi istražiti tko je sve bio prije nas.
sections.subtitle_en: 1360 surnames that flew under the radar
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host Kruno speaks about his book on surnames and the weak public interest
sections.content_en:
Kruno reveals that he was disappointed that many people are not interested in this topic. For ten years he worked on a doctoral dissertation that, among other things, deals with the first names and surnames of his region, **Poklončićko prigorje**. From that work, the book **"Prezimena Poklončićkog prigorja"** also emerged. He thought that people would "snatch it up." He was not counting on profit, but on interest. Nevertheless, the book "flew under the radar": only here and there does someone ask about it or look up their surname.

In the book, he covered **1360 surnames**, with their first occurrence, spelling, meaning, etymology, and motivation. Surnames, he says, are so interesting and tell so much, yet many "do not care." Kruno believes that a person must know where they came from because in a way that also shows where they are going. Origin does not delineate the path, but it is a great incentive. Still, Fran's and other similar stories encourage him that he was not writing only for himself.

Fran draws attention to a phenomenon in **America**, where a whole wave of **genealogy** researchers is growing. There, everyone came from somewhere, and many do not know where from. He believes that this will gradually happen in Croatia as well, because we all think that we are "only" what we are. He thought that all his ancestors were Slavonians, but it turned out that they were Czechs. "We are all from somewhere."

From his research, he also drew a great lesson. One should be proud of one's origin, but **not superficially**. Every lineage carries its burden, even the "sins of antiquity." On the other hand, one should not live under that burden either, because we can no longer influence ancient times. What we can do is thank God for everyone who existed and allowed the next one to be born, all the way to us. If just one person had not been in that chain, "we probably would not exist." That, says the guest, is a miracle, and precisely because of that it is worth investigating who all came before us.

sections.subtitle: Prijatelj koji je nakon 25 godina stao na očev grob
sections.screenshot_description: Fran prepričava dirljivu priču o prijatelju koji je pronašao oca
sections.content:
Fran dijeli i „friški događaj“. Nedavno je upoznao čovjeka koji ga je dočekao u jednom mjestu. Kad mu je rekao kako se preziva, Fran je odgovorio: „Čovječe, pa moja se šukunbaka tako prezivala.“ Pitao ga je je li iz tog i tog kraja, i bio je. Novi poznanik priznao mu je da ima složenu situaciju. To je majčino prezime, a oca nikad nije upoznao. Majka o tome nije voljela govoriti, a njega je to mučilo cijeli život, više od 25 godina.

Fran mu je rekao što bi sam napravio na njegovu mjestu, jer ima neke resurse. Nakon tri mjeseca prijatelj mu se javio: „Slušaj, bio sam prekjučer na grobu svog oca.“ Oca je pronašao u **drugoj državi**. Saznao je njegovo ime i prezime i prvi put u životu vidio ljude koji nalikuju na njega i nose isto prezime.

Gost priznaje da je nakon toga bio dva dana pod dojmom. Netko je zbog njihova razgovora smogao snage otići toliko daleko, u drugu državu, da otkrije istinu. Tu je ponovno vidio koliko je važno otkriti identitet za kojim je netko tragao cijeli život, „barem taj zemaljski identitet“.

Kruno zaključuje da je **identitet** jedno od najvažnijih pitanja čovječanstva. Kad čovjek sazna tko je, to mu je „velik vjetar u leđa“.
sections.subtitle_en: A friend who stood at his father's grave after 25 years
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fran recounts a touching story about a friend who found his father
sections.content_en:
Fran also shares a “recent event”. He recently met a man who welcomed him in a certain place. When he told him what his last name was, Fran replied: “Man, my great-great-grandmother had that last name.” He asked him if he was from such-and-such an area, and he was. The new acquaintance admitted to him that he had a complex situation. That is his mother's last name, and he had never met his father. His mother did not like to speak about it, and it had troubled him his whole life, for more than 25 years.

Fran told him what he would do in his place, because he has some resources. After three months, the friend contacted him: “Listen, the day before yesterday I was at my father's grave.” He found his father in **another country**. He learned his first and last name and, for the first time in his life, saw people who resemble him and bear the same last name.

The guest admits that after that he was deeply moved for two days. Because of their conversation, someone found the strength to go that far, to another country, to uncover the truth. There he saw once again how important it is to discover the identity someone had been searching for their whole life, “at least that earthly identity”.

Kruno concludes that **identity** is one of the most important questions of humanity. When a person finds out who he is, that gives him a “great wind at his back”.

sections.subtitle: Blic „ili-ili“, „Ne bojte se!“ i poruka nade za kraj
sections.screenshot_description: Gost preporučuje knjigu i upućuje poruku mladim muškarcima
sections.content:
Pred kraj Kruno uvodi „blitzkrieg“ pet kratkih **„ili-ili“ pitanja**. Napominje da su neka „tricky“, a neka možda i komična, te da gost slobodno smije odbiti obje opcije. Franovi odgovori:
- **Inspiracija ili disciplina?** Inspiracija.
- **Raditi noću ili ujutro?** Ujutro.
- **Božja pobjeda ili Prdavci?** Uz uzvik „O, čovječe!“ i šalu da ovisi o okolnostima, Božja pobjeda. Kruno to komentira kao „mudro“.
- **Sestre Halužan ili sestre Palić?** Sestre Halužan, iz sentimentalnih razloga, jer su mu bile „desne ruke“ na snimanju pjesme. Dodaje da se sestre Palić ne trebaju uvrijediti jer ga „Kornelija i ekipa“ dobro znaju. Kruno gledatelje poziva da pogledaju spot.
- **Kreativni kaos ili uredna struktura?** Kreativni kaos.

Za kraj Kruno traži poruku mladim muškarcima bilo kojeg poziva koji imaju snove, ali se boje odvažiti. Fran preporučuje knjigu **„Sanjajte i snovi će nadići realnost“**. Napisao ju je prijatelj **svetog Josemaríje Escrive**, a temelji se na istinitom događaju. Govori o poticajima koje je Escrivá imao prije osnivanja **Opusa Dei**, Djela Božjeg. Djelo je nastalo iz jedne ideje u razmatranju, a danas je, kako kaže Fran, velika struktura u Crkvi i „dobra kičma muževnosti u Crkvi“. Svoju poruku sažima riječima pape **Ivana Pavla II.**: **„Ne bojte se!“** Kruno dodaje „Uzmi i čitaj“, a gost se slaže.

Kruno zahvaljuje gostu na svjedočanstvu i bogatom iskustvu za koje vjeruje da je progovorilo mnogima. Fran zahvaljuje na pozivu i poželi da svaki podcast bude „ovako slojevit i šaljiv na kraju“. Voditelj se zatim oprašta od publike i poziva je da podcast podrže na **Patreonu**, gdje mogu već danas pogledati sljedeću epizodu.

Nakon odjave slijedi kratak isječak s porukom nade: **„Nisi sam. Nisi sam i može biti bolje.“** U njemu se ističe da je mnogima bolje nego prije, nakon što su prošli program, i da nitko od onih koji su ga prošli nije zažalio, nego su „našli mir“.
sections.subtitle_en: Flash 'either-or', 'Do not be afraid!' and a message of hope for the end
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest recommends a book and addresses a message to young men
sections.content_en:
Towards the end, Kruno introduces a 'blitzkrieg' of five short **'either-or' questions**. He notes that some are 'tricky', and some perhaps even comical, and that the guest is freely allowed to reject both options. Fran's answers:
- **Inspiration or discipline?** Inspiration.
- **Working at night or in the morning?** In the morning.
- **Božja pobjeda or Prdavci?** With an exclamation of 'Oh, man!' and a joke that it depends on the circumstances, Božja pobjeda. Kruno comments on this as 'wise'.
- **Sestre Halužan or sestre Palić?** Sestre Halužan, for sentimental reasons, because they were his 'right hands' during the recording of the song. He adds that sestre Palić should not be offended because 'Kornelija and the crew' know him well. Kruno invites the viewers to watch the music video.
- **Creative chaos or orderly structure?** Creative chaos.

For the end, Kruno asks for a message to young men of any vocation who have dreams, but are afraid to dare. Fran recommends the book **'Dream and Dreams Will Transcend Reality'**. It was written by a friend of **Saint Josemaría Escrivá**, and is based on a true event. It speaks about the promptings that Escrivá had before founding **Opus Dei**, the Work of God. The Work originated from one idea in contemplation, and today it is, as Fran says, a large structure in the Church and 'a good backbone of masculinity in the Church'. He summarizes his message with the words of Pope **John Paul II**: **'Do not be afraid!'** Kruno adds 'Take and read', and the guest agrees.

Kruno thanks the guest for his testimony and the rich experience that he believes spoke to many. Fran gives thanks for the invitation and wishes that every podcast would be 'this layered and humorous at the end'. The host then says goodbye to the audience and invites them to support the podcast on **Patreon**, where they can already watch the next episode today.

After the sign-off, a short clip follows with a message of hope: **'You are not alone. You are not alone and it can be better.'** In it, it is emphasized that many are doing better than before, after having gone through the program, and that none of those who went through it have regretted it, but rather they 'found peace'.

iterations.theme_en: Fran Petar Reizl: entrepreneurship, family, faith, music, and the search for family roots
